# Gram

> Gram is an open-source declarative and computational recipe DSL built for developers. Code your recipes in plain text: `.gram` files compile into structured, calculated JSON — with relational variables, physical-accuracy shopping lists, modular imports (@use), and strict data contracts for temperatures, times, ingredients, and cookware.

Gram is a pipeline of composable `@gram-lang/*` npm packages (`parser`, `kitchen`, `analyzer`, `renderer`, `format`, `i18n`), plus a `gram` CLI, a Language Server, and a VS Code extension. Full documentation is at https://gram-lang.org/ (with a French translation under `/fr/`). For the complete language spec in a single file, see https://gram-lang.org/llms-full.txt.

## Getting Started

- [What is Gram?](https://gram-lang.org/docs/explanation/philosophy): Project origin and vision — recipes as code, relational logic, and data integrity.
- [Getting Started](https://gram-lang.org/docs/tutorials/getting-started): Installing the Gram CLI/ecosystem and compiling your first recipe.
- [Your First Complex Recipe](https://gram-lang.org/docs/tutorials/first-recipe): A full walkthrough using intermediates, timers, and scaling.

## Syntax Reference

- [Document Structure](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/syntax/document-structure): Frontmatter, sections, steps, and comments.
- [Ingredients](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/syntax/ingredients): `@ingredient` declarations, quantities, units, and modifiers.
- [Cookware](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/syntax/cookware): `#cookware` declarations and quantities.
- [Times & Scheduling](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/syntax/times): `~timer` declarations, active vs. passive, and section retro-planning.
- [Temperatures](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/syntax/temperatures): `^temperature` declarations, exact and semantic.
- [Intermediate Variables](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/syntax/intermediate-variables): Declaring and referencing sub-components (`->&name`) like dough or sauce across steps.
- [Relative Quantities](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/syntax/relative-quantities): Defining a quantity as a dynamic percentage of another ingredient or variable.
- [Composite Ingredients](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/syntax/composite-ingredients): `<@parent` syntax so sub-parts (zest/juice) aggregate correctly in the shopping list.
- [Cheatsheet](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/syntax/cheatsheet): One-page quick reference for all syntax elements and modifiers.
- [Writing Gram Programmatically](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/syntax/ai-generation-notes): Guidance and common mistakes for scripts/AI models generating `.gram` files.

## API Reference

- [API Overview](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/api/): The pipeline of composable packages and install instructions.
- [@gram-lang/parser](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/api/parser): `getAST()` — turns `.gram` source into a plain-object AST.
- [@gram-lang/kitchen](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/api/kitchen): `compile()` — produces the shopping list, timings, registry, and warnings.
- [@gram-lang/analyzer](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/api/analyzer): `analyze()` — enriches a compiled recipe with mass, yield, nutrition, and baker's percentages.
- [@gram-lang/renderer](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/api/renderer): Rendering a compiled/analyzed result to Markdown or HTML.
- [@gram-lang/format](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/api/format): `formatGram()` — canonical code formatter with 13 unified formatting rules.
- [@gram-lang/i18n](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/api/i18n): Unit/time normalization and localization dictionaries.
- [Data Formats](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/api/data-formats): The JSON shapes flowing between pipeline stages, and the ingredient database YAML schema.
- [Warnings](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/api/warnings): The `Warning` interface, all warning codes, and `--strict` severity.

## Guides

- [How to Manage an Ingredient Database](https://gram-lang.org/docs/how-to/manage-database): Sync, lint, and enrich a local `ingredients.yaml` via the CLI.
- [How to Scale Recipes Dynamically](https://gram-lang.org/docs/how-to/scale-recipes): Relative quantities and baker's math for ratio-based recipes.
- [How to Generate a Weekly Shopping List](https://gram-lang.org/docs/how-to/weekly-shopping-list): Aggregating ingredients across multiple `.gram` files with `gram shop`.
- [How to Build a Custom UI](https://gram-lang.org/docs/how-to/build-custom-ui): Consuming Gram's compiled JSON to build a custom frontend.

## Optional

- [Playground](https://gram-lang.org/play): Interactive in-browser editor with a live compiler preview.
- [CLI Commands](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/tooling/cli): Reference for the `gram` command-line tool.
- [VS Code Extension](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/tooling/vscode-extension): Live preview, nutrition CodeLens, ingredient matching.
- [Language Server](https://gram-lang.org/docs/reference/tooling/language-server): The LSP implementation powering editor integrations.
- [The Gram Lifecycle](https://gram-lang.org/docs/explanation/engine/lifecycle): How the parser → kitchen → analyzer → renderer pipeline fits together.
- [Deep Dive: Mass Standardization & Yield](https://gram-lang.org/docs/explanation/mass-and-yield): Converting volumes/counts to standardized mass.
- [Deep Dive: Nutritional Estimation](https://gram-lang.org/docs/explanation/nutrition): The macro/micronutrient calculation flow.
- [Deep Dive: Shopping List Aggregation](https://gram-lang.org/docs/explanation/shopping-list-aggregation): ID normalization, alias resolution, and unit merging.
- [Deep Dive: Scaling](https://gram-lang.org/docs/explanation/scaling): The three scaling mechanisms unified through the `ScaleEngine`.
